metadata.sources: Verified via web search, organizational websites, academic papers, news reports, Wikipedia

case_studies.title: Kiva: Crowdfunded Microloans
case_studies.problem_statement: Lack of access to capital for the poor
case_studies.the_model: Peer-to-peer crowdfunded microloans via web platform. Average loan: $411.
what_worked: Storytelling model created emotional donor connection
Low default rate proved model works
what_didnt_work: Most loans pre-disbursed by field partners
case_studies.key_lesson: The story IS the product. People give money to people they connect with.

case_studies.title: GiveDirectly: Just Give People Money
case_studies.problem_statement: Extreme poverty; traditional aid overhead
case_studies.the_model: Unconditional cash transfers ($1,000/household) via mobile money.
what_worked: RCTs proved cash transfers increase consumption, assets
case_studies.key_lesson: The poor know what they need better than any NGO. Trust people with cash.

case_studies.title: Zipline: Drones That Save Mothers' Lives
case_studies.problem_statement: Rural hospitals run out of blood, vaccines, medicines
case_studies.the_model: Autonomous drone delivery of medical supplies. WhatsApp ordering.
case_studies.key_lesson: When the problem is life-or-death, speed is the product. Find your '61% faster' metric.

case_studies.title: Tala: Your Phone Is Your Credit Score
case_studies.problem_statement: 3B+ underbanked adults lack credit access
case_studies.the_model: Mobile app uses smartphone data for credit scoring. Microloans in minutes.
what_worked: Alternative credit scoring via phone usage
case_studies.key_lesson: Your phone knows more about your reliability than your bank does. Find the hidden data.

case_studies.title: charity: water: 100% Model That Raised $700M
case_studies.problem_statement: 770M people lack clean water. Donor trust gap.
case_studies.the_model: 100% model: every public dollar funds water. GPS on every well.
what_worked: Radical transparency — GPS on every well
what_didnt_work: Sustainability of water projects in some regions
Requires wealthy private donors for operations
case_studies.key_lesson: Trust is the product. Build verification into the product from day one.

case_studies.title: M-KOPA: Pay-As-You-Go Solar for 7M Families
case_studies.problem_statement: 600M+ Africans lack electricity; can't afford upfront solar
case_studies.the_model: Pay-as-you-go solar via daily M-Pesa micropayments. IoT asset locking.
case_studies.key_lesson: Match payment to income pattern. Daily workers need daily payments.

case_studies.title: d.light: Killing Kerosene with $10 Solar Lamps
case_studies.problem_statement: 1.3B people without electricity; kerosene health hazards
case_studies.the_model: Affordable solar lanterns ($10-50) sold retail and via PAYG financing.
what_worked: Shift from retail to PAYG financing
what_didnt_work: Early retail model had high customer acquisition costs
case_studies.key_lesson: Start with the simplest possible product. The $10 lantern proved the model before scaling up.

case_studies.title: One Acre Fund: $75 That Lifts Farmers Out of Poverty
case_studies.problem_statement: Smallholder farmers can't afford seeds and fertilizer at planting time
case_studies.the_model: $75 loan for bundled seed, fertilizer, 8 training sessions, market access.
what_worked: Field officer model at village level
what_didnt_work: Dependence on donor funding for expansion
case_studies.key_lesson: Bundle the service. Seeds alone fail. Training alone fails. Together, they work.

case_studies.title: Andela: Training Africa's Engineers for Global Tech
case_studies.problem_statement: Africa has brilliant engineers but no pathway to global tech jobs
case_studies.the_model: Train developers for 6 months, connect to global companies. Income-sharing model.
case_studies.key_lesson: Genius is evenly distributed. Opportunity is not. Remove the geography, unlock the talent.

case_studies.title: Living Goods: Smartphones for 12,000 Health Workers
case_studies.problem_statement: Preventable child and maternal deaths in rural Africa
case_studies.the_model: Train CHWs with smartphones, medicines, diagnostics. Door-to-door care.
case_studies.key_lesson: Don't replace the system — strengthen it. Put smartphones in hands of women already walking door to door.

case_studies.title: KickStart: $180 Pumps That Lifted 1.7M Out of Poverty
case_studies.problem_statement: Rain-dependent farming traps millions in poverty
case_studies.the_model: Design and sell low-cost irrigation pumps ($180) through local retail.
case_studies.key_lesson: Sell, don't give. Selling proves value. Donating proves need.

case_studies.title: LifeBank: Blood Delivered in Under 1 Hour
case_studies.problem_statement: Maternal deaths from blood shortages; hospitals can't find blood banks
case_studies.the_model: Platform connects blood banks to hospitals. Delivers blood via motorcycles and drones.
case_studies.key_lesson: The founder's story IS the pitch. Personal pain creates authentic purpose.

case_studies.title: Evidence Action: $0.50 Per Child to Deworm the World
case_studies.problem_statement: 1.5B children infected with intestinal worms
case_studies.the_model: Government partnerships for mass school-based deworming at $0.50/child.
case_studies.key_lesson: Find the $0.50 solution. Do the cheap thing first.

case_studies.title: Ushahidi: Citizens Mapping Crisis in 150 Countries
case_studies.problem_statement: No tool for citizens to report violence/crisis events in real-time
case_studies.the_model: Open-source crowdsourcing platform. SMS/email/web reports on public maps.
case_studies.key_lesson: A simple tech layer on citizen reporting can replace expensive surveillance infrastructure.

case_studies.title: BRAC: 100,000 Women on Bicycles Changing Bangladesh
case_studies.problem_statement: Extreme poverty; ultra-poor too poor for microfinance
case_studies.the_model: Sequenced package: asset transfer, skills training, weekly coaching, savings, healthcare.
case_studies.key_lesson: The human element — a neighbor who shows up every week — is the irreplaceable ingredient.

case_studies.title: ASHA Workers: One Million Women Walking Door to Door
case_studies.problem_statement: Rural India has clinics but no connection between clinics and villages
case_studies.the_model: One million+ women, one per ~1,000 population. Local woman connects village to health system.
what_worked: She is from the village, speaks the language, knows every family
case_studies.key_lesson: A woman from the village who speaks the language is more effective than any outside expert.

case_studies.title: Kenya's Free Pads in Schools
case_studies.problem_statement: 1 in 10 girls misses school every month because of her period
case_studies.the_model: Government legislated free pads in all public schools. Combined with education.

impact_numbers.policy: Free pads in all public schools

what_didnt_work: Pads alone did NOT improve attendance (Harvard RCT)
case_studies.key_lesson: Breaking the taboo matters as much as the product. Education IS the infrastructure.

case_studies.title: CLTS: Making Communities Disgusted With Themselves
case_studies.problem_statement: 394 million people practice open defecation
case_studies.the_model: Facilitator triggers collective disgust. Community builds own latrines. No subsidies.

impact_numbers.behavior_change: Open defecation decreased in all evaluations

what_worked: No subsidy — community invests own resources
what_didnt_work: Shame can be harmful if not managed
Doesn't work in all cultural contexts
case_studies.key_lesson: When the community decides together, behavior change sticks. Don't build for them. Trigger them to build.

case_studies.title: Minna no Kai: Japan's 50-Year Community Elder Care
case_studies.problem_statement: Japan's elderly live alone. Traditional care systems breaking down.
case_studies.the_model: Neighbors checking on neighbors. Volunteer drivers. Shared meals. Community salons.
what_didnt_work: Aging volunteers — who cares for caregivers?
case_studies.key_lesson: The solution is already there — it's called 'being a neighbor.' Formalize the informal.

case_studies.title: Conditional Cash Transfers: Paying Families to Keep Girls in School
case_studies.problem_statement: 12 million girls married before 18 each year. Economic pressure drives child marriage.
case_studies.the_model: Pay families $10-50/month to keep daughters enrolled. Conditional on attendance.
what_worked: Economic pressure drives child marriage — removing it works
what_didnt_work: Education alone without financial support has weaker effects
case_studies.key_lesson: Economic pressure drives child marriage. Removing that pressure works. Pay them to stay.

case_studies.title: KATARIBA: Diagonal Relationships That Save Japanese Youth
case_studies.problem_statement: Japanese teens have among the lowest self-esteem globally
case_studies.the_model: Four pillars: DISCOVER, RESILIENCE, GLOCAL, POST-TRAUMATIC GROWTH. Diagonal relationships.
what_worked: Diagonal relationships — older peers, not parents/teachers
case_studies.key_lesson: Don't fight the system. Build alongside it. KATARIBA built a parallel path for kids the system abandoned.

case_studies.title: ETIC.: Japan's Social Entrepreneur Ecosystem
case_studies.problem_statement: Japan lacked infrastructure for social entrepreneurs
case_studies.the_model: Ecosystem builder: MAKERS UNIVERSITY, Tokyo Startup Gateway, Social Entrepreneurship School.
what_worked: Ecosystem approach — pipeline from idea to scale
case_studies.key_lesson: Don't build one startup — build the infrastructure for 1,000 startups.

case_studies.title: Civic Force: 24-Hour Disaster Response from Japan
case_studies.problem_statement: Japan's disasters lack coordinated private-sector + NPO rapid-response
case_studies.the_model: Coordination body deploying helicopters and teams within 24 hours.
case_studies.key_lesson: Be the coordinator, not the executor. The connector is the most valuable player.

case_studies.title: Silver Human Resource Centers: Japan's Elder Employment
case_studies.problem_statement: Japan's aging population needs meaningful employment and social connection
case_studies.the_model: Government-supported membership organizations offering light work for seniors 60+.
what_worked: Focus on social connection, not just income
what_didnt_work: Matching seniors with skilled positions difficult
case_studies.key_lesson: The problem isn't just money — it's meaning. Address the emotional need, not just the economic one.

case_studies.title: Peace Boat: 60,000+ Participants for Peace
case_studies.problem_statement: Promoting peace, human rights, sustainability through experiential education
case_studies.the_model: Global voyages combining travel with peace-building workshops and SDG education.
what_didnt_work: Limited to those who can travel
case_studies.key_lesson: Experiential education creates lasting change. Visit the problem, don't just read about it.

case_studies.title: Panzi Hospital: 30,000 Survivors of Sexual Violence
case_studies.problem_statement: Sexual violence as weapon of war in eastern DRC
case_studies.the_model: Holistic 'one-stop center': medical treatment, psychosocial support, legal assistance, reintegration.
what_worked: Holistic one-stop model became global reference
Dr. Mukwege's Nobel Prize elevated the issue
case_studies.key_lesson: The one-stop model proves that medical care alone isn't enough. Survivors need legal, psychological, and community support together.

case_studies.title: HEAL Africa: Teaching Hospital in War-Torn Goma
case_studies.problem_statement: Medical and social needs in war-torn eastern DRC
case_studies.the_model: Community hospital providing surgical care, psychosocial support, community development.
case_studies.key_lesson: Local ownership creates trust that no outside organization can replicate. The hospital belongs to the community.

case_studies.title: Eastern Congo Initiative: Local Organizations, Global Advocacy
case_studies.problem_statement: Lack of international attention and funding for eastern Congo
case_studies.the_model: Grant-making initiative funding local Congolese organizations rather than implementing directly.
case_studies.key_lesson: Fund the locals, don't replace them. They know the context better than any outsider.

case_studies.title: Women for Women International: 12-Month Empowerment
case_studies.problem_statement: Extreme gender inequality and sexual violence in conflict zones
case_studies.the_model: 12-month program: rights awareness, vocational skills, business training, peer support.

impact_numbers.impact: Significant increases in savings, assets, empowerment

case_studies.key_lesson: RCT evidence is the most powerful fundraising tool. Prove it works with data, not stories.

case_studies.title: Mercy Corps DRC: 1.2 Million People in One Year
case_studies.problem_statement: Humanitarian crisis: displacement, food insecurity, Ebola, conflict
case_studies.the_model: Multi-sector response: clean water, livelihoods, nutrition, Ebola response, WASH.
case_studies.key_lesson: In crisis, the ability to scale fast matters more than perfect planning.

case_studies.title: Flutterwave: Africa's Payment Rails
case_studies.problem_statement: Fragmented payment infrastructure across Africa
case_studies.the_model: Unified payment API enabling businesses to accept payments across 34+ countries.
case_studies.key_lesson: Build the rails, not the train. Infrastructure enables everything else.

case_studies.title: Piggyvest: 6 Million Nigerians Saving Money
case_studies.problem_statement: Only 2% of Nigerians save formally
case_studies.the_model: Automated savings platform with lock features, goal-based savings.
what_worked: Annual savings report became cultural phenomenon
case_studies.key_lesson: Make saving social. When everyone shares their savings report, saving becomes a status symbol.

case_studies.title: Moniepoint: Banking Nigeria's Informal Economy
case_studies.problem_statement: 60M+ informal businesses lack access to digital payments
case_studies.the_model: Agent banking network: POS terminals, business accounts, lending to informal merchants.

impact_numbers.profitable: First African fintech profitable at unicorn scale

what_worked: Hardware + software bundle created sticky relationships
case_studies.key_lesson: The informal market is the market. 60M businesses that banks ignored are now Moniepoint's customers.

case_studies.title: CcHUB: Africa's Largest Innovation Hub
case_studies.problem_statement: Nigeria's tech ecosystem lacked collaboration space
case_studies.the_model: Innovation hub: co-working, accelerator programs, venture building.
what_worked: Gravitational center of Lagos tech ecosystem
case_studies.key_lesson: Be the gravity. When the ecosystem orbits around you, everything grows.

case_studies.title: Tony Elumelu Foundation: $100M for 24,000 Entrepreneurs
case_studies.problem_statement: Africa's entrepreneurs lack seed capital, mentorship, training
case_studies.the_model: $5,000 seed capital + 12-week training + mentorship. Non-refundable grant.
case_studies.key_lesson: Non-refundable grants remove the fear of failure. When you don't have to pay it back, you take bigger risks.

case_studies.title: Farmcrowdy: Crowdfunding Nigerian Farms
case_studies.problem_statement: 38M smallholder farmers lack access to capital and markets
case_studies.the_model: Digital platform connecting investors with farmers. Investors fund farm cycles.
what_worked: Crowdfunding attracted urban Nigerians as farm investors
what_didnt_work: Pivoted from crowdfunding to B2B agri-commerce
case_studies.key_lesson: Connect the city to the farm. Urban investors fund rural farmers. Both benefit.

case_studies.title: Gawad Kalinga: 70,000+ Homes Built by Communities
case_studies.problem_statement: Millions of Filipino families live in unsafe informal settlements
case_studies.the_model: Community-driven housing: corporations, volunteers, and families co-build villages.
what_worked: Holistic approach — housing + education + health + livelihood
case_studies.key_lesson: Housing alone isn't enough. A home without education, health, and livelihood is just a building.

case_studies.title: Teach for the Philippines: Cross-Sector Teachers
case_studies.problem_statement: Filipino students face severe learning gaps. Many graduate functionally illiterate.
case_studies.the_model: Recruit professionals from diverse fields to teach in underserved schools for 2 years.
what_worked: Alumni network became education policy pipeline
what_didnt_work: Small scale vs. national teacher shortage
case_studies.key_lesson: The best teachers aren't always trained teachers. Cross-sector recruitment brings fresh energy.

case_studies.title: Rags2Riches: Turning Trash Into Premium Fashion
case_studies.problem_statement: Women in Payatas dumpsite earn below minimum wage from scrap materials
case_studies.the_model: Social enterprise upcycling scrap cloth into premium fashion accessories.
what_worked: Premium positioning transformed 'trash' into aspirational products
what_didnt_work: Scaling artisan production while maintaining quality
case_studies.key_lesson: Position determines price. The same scrap cloth, positioned as premium, pays living wages.

case_studies.title: Liter of Light: Solar Lighting for 382,000+ Filipinos
case_studies.problem_statement: Millions lack access to electricity in off-grid and disaster-affected communities
case_studies.the_model: Grassroots movement teaching communities to build solar lighting from local materials.
what_didnt_work: Scaling to complex systems needed engineering
case_studies.key_lesson: Teach them to build it themselves. A community that can make its own lights doesn't need you anymore.

case_studies.title: Hapinoy: Empowering 800,000 Corner Stores
case_studies.problem_statement: 800,000+ sari-sari stores lack business skills, financing, supply chain
case_studies.the_model: Micro-enterprise development: training, aggregation, digitization of corner store owners.
what_worked: Trusted store owners as community distribution points
case_studies.key_lesson: The corner store is the community hub. Empower the store owner, empower the neighborhood.

case_studies.title: Kiron: Free University for Refugees
case_studies.problem_statement: Refugees excluded from higher education
case_studies.the_model: Free online degree pathways partnering with universities.
what_worked: Transition from NGO to social business with employer-funded programs
what_didnt_work: Early grant dependence created sustainability challenges
case_studies.key_lesson: Refugees aren't just beneficiaries — they're talent. Train them, employ them, transform them.

case_studies.title: Sozialhelden: 3.2M Venue Entries for Wheelchair Accessibility
case_studies.problem_statement: Urban inaccessibility for wheelchair users
case_studies.the_model: Crowdsourced platform (Wheelmap.org) + disability consulting.
what_worked: Open-data approach scaled globally without heavy infrastructure
what_didnt_work: Crowdsourced data quality varies by region
case_studies.key_lesson: Crowdsourcing turns users into builders. The community builds the product for you.

case_studies.title: BonVenture: Impact VC in DACH Region
case_studies.problem_statement: Social enterprises lack access to venture capital
case_studies.the_model: Impact venture capital fund across DACH region.
what_worked: Blended 'true impact and return' model attracted mainstream investors
what_didnt_work: Smaller deal sizes vs. traditional VC limit fundraising
case_studies.key_lesson: Impact and return aren't opposites. Prove both, and mainstream investors will follow.

case_studies.title: Teach First Deutschland: Fellows at Disadvantaged Schools
case_studies.problem_statement: Educational inequality at under-resourced schools
case_studies.the_model: Two-year fellowships placing top graduates at Brennpunktschulen.
what_worked: Corporate partnerships provided sustainable funding pipeline
what_didnt_work: Fellows leave after two years — continuity gaps
case_studies.key_lesson: Two years is enough to change a child's trajectory. Even temporary excellence matters.

case_studies.title: Viva con Agua: Water Projects Through Music and Football
case_studies.organization: Viva con Agua de Sankt Pauli
case_studies.problem_statement: 696M people lack safe drinking water
case_studies.the_model: Festival/event-based fundraising + WASH project delivery. From FC St. Pauli fan community.
what_worked: Culture-first approach attracted demographics traditional NGOs miss
what_didnt_work: Event revenue is volatile and hard to predict
case_studies.key_lesson: Meet people where they are. If they're at a concert, make the concert the fundraiser.

case_studies.title: betterplace.org: Germany's Largest Donation Platform
case_studies.problem_statement: Donor trust gap and fragmented charitable giving
case_studies.the_model: Germany's largest donation platform connecting donors directly to verified projects.
what_didnt_work: Platform fees create tension with smaller NPOs
case_studies.key_lesson: Transparency is a feature, not a nice-to-have. Show donors exactly where their money goes.

case_studies.title: Instituto Ayrton Senna: 36 Million Students Reached
case_studies.problem_statement: Brazil's education system fails millions of children
case_studies.the_model: Partners with public school systems for teacher training, curriculum, policy advocacy.
what_didnt_work: Education outcomes still poor despite scale
case_studies.key_lesson: Legacy can scale. One person's story, properly channeled, can reach 36 million students.

case_studies.title: Gerando Falcoes: Tech-Enabled Favela Development
case_studies.problem_statement: Intergenerational poverty in Brazil's favelas (16M+ people)
case_studies.the_model: Tech-enabled community development: education, employment, 'Smart Slums' infrastructure.
what_worked: Founder's authentic favela background builds trust
case_studies.key_lesson: Authenticity is the ultimate trust signal. Growing up in the favela gives credibility no outsider can buy.

case_studies.title: Gastromotiva: Social Gastronomy Movement
case_studies.problem_statement: Youth unemployment and food insecurity in favelas
case_studies.the_model: Professional culinary training for vulnerable youth. Community kitchens. Solidary Kitchens.
what_worked: Gastronomy as accessible entry point for social mobility
Rio 2016 Olympics RefettoRio raised global profile
what_didnt_work: Culinary training alone doesn't address structural unemployment
case_studies.key_lesson: Food is the universal language. Everyone eats. Use gastronomy as the entry point for social change.

case_studies.title: Instituto Sou da Paz: Evidence-Based Violence Prevention
case_studies.problem_statement: Brazil's epidemic: ~50,000 homicides annually
case_studies.the_model: Evidence-based violence prevention: arms control advocacy, community policing reform.
what_worked: Evidence-based approach built credibility with policymakers
Focus on firearms reduction showed measurable impact
what_didnt_work: Political shifts can reverse policy gains
case_studies.key_lesson: Evidence beats ideology. When you show the data, policymakers listen.

case_studies.title: Laboratoria: Coding Bootcamp for Low-Income Women
case_studies.problem_statement: Gender gap in tech; women from low-income backgrounds excluded
case_studies.the_model: Intensive 6-month coding bootcamp. Job placement support. Employer partnerships.
what_worked: High job placement rates prove the model
Employer partnerships ensure graduates get hired
case_studies.key_lesson: Placement rate is the metric that matters. 80%+ placement proves the training works.

case_studies.title: Konfio: AI Credit Scoring for Mexican SMEs
case_studies.problem_statement: ~50% of Mexican adults unbanked; SMEs rejected by banks
case_studies.the_model: Fintech platform using alternative data and AI for credit scoring.
what_worked: Technology-driven underwriting reduced risk and cost
what_didnt_work: High interest rates typical of subprime lending
case_studies.key_lesson: The 'unbankable' are bankable — you just need better data to see it.

case_studies.title: Kueski: BNPL for Mexico's Unbanked
case_studies.problem_statement: Majority of Mexicans lack access to traditional consumer credit
case_studies.the_model: Consumer lending + 'Kueski Pay' BNPL for e-commerce. Alternative credit scoring via mobile data.

impact_numbers.approach: BNPL tapped into Mexico's growing e-commerce

case_studies.key_lesson: Match the payment method to the shopping method. E-commerce needs e-payments.

case_studies.title: Habitat for Humanity Mexico: Sweat Equity Housing
case_studies.problem_statement: Millions of Mexicans live in inadequate housing
case_studies.the_model: Affordable housing construction. Microfinance for housing. 'Sweat equity' model.

impact_numbers.approach: Built and improved thousands of homes

what_didnt_work: Individual building doesn't address systemic issues
case_studies.key_lesson: Sweat equity creates ownership. When you build your own home, you take care of it forever.

case_studies.title: Barefoot College: Training Illiterate Women as Solar Engineers
case_studies.problem_statement: Rural communities excluded from modern technology due to illiteracy and poverty.
case_studies.the_model: Train illiterate and semi-literate villagers, primarily women, as solar engineers and water pump technicians. Night schools, visual learning with no literacy requirements. Village committees select trainees and set prices.
what_worked: Women as solar engineers and community leaders
Locally led initiatives where villages select trainees
Visual learning methods requiring no literacy
UNESCO, UNDP, and Indian government partnerships
what_didnt_work: Returned Aga Khan Award over crediting controversy
Wikipedia article flagged for promotional content
case_studies.key_lesson: Rural communities can manage advanced technology with appropriate training. Education must be practical and aligned with local needs.

case_studies.title: Pratham: Teaching at the Right Level for 34 Million Children
case_studies.problem_statement: 50% of children in Indian government schools cannot read, write, or do basic arithmetic after 4-5 years of schooling.
case_studies.the_model: Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) groups students by assessed learning level rather than age. Community volunteers, pre-school classes, the Annual Status of Education Report (ASER) household survey, and vocational training.
what_worked: ASER shifted Indian education policy from inputs to outcomes, adapted by 14 countries
TaRL recommended as 'Good Buy' by Global Education Evidence Advisory Panel
GiveWell top charity in developing-world education
what_didnt_work: Half of government school children still lacked basic literacy despite interventions
case_studies.key_lesson: Group children by current learning level, not age. Measurable outcomes matter more than enrollment numbers.

case_studies.title: Goonj: Urban Surplus as a Development Tool
case_studies.problem_statement: Clothing is an overlooked basic need. Urban surplus goes to waste while rural communities lack cloth and sanitary supplies.
case_studies.the_model: Cloth for Work: villagers work on community projects in exchange for material resources. Recycled cloth turned into affordable sanitary pads at 2 rupees each. School-to-school supply exchanges.
what_worked: Cloth for Work dignifies recipients as workers not charity cases
Addressing menstrual hygiene through affordable recycled pads
what_didnt_work: Depends on continuous urban material supply and logistics infrastructure
case_studies.key_lesson: Clothing is a critical neglected humanitarian need. Treating recipients as contributors preserves dignity.

case_studies.title: Sulabh International: Sanitation Revolution Without Sewerage
case_studies.problem_statement: Lack of sanitation and the degrading practice of manual scavenging perpetuating caste-based inequality.
case_studies.the_model: Two-pit pour-flush toilet that works without sewerage infrastructure. Pay-and-use public toilets with bath, laundry, and urinal facilities. Biogas conversion from human waste.
what_worked: Simple, affordable toilet technology without sewerage
UN Habitat II 'Urban Best Practice' recognition
what_didnt_work: Criticized for 'patronising methods' dealing with caste-based sanitation work
Technology alone cannot solve entrenched caste attitudes
case_studies.key_lesson: Affordable appropriate technology can solve massive infrastructure gaps. Sanitation is a dignity issue intertwined with caste and class.

case_studies.title: Akshaya Patra: 4 Billion Meals for School Children
case_studies.problem_statement: Children miss education because of hunger. Malnutrition drives school dropout rates.
case_studies.the_model: Implements India's PM POSHAN scheme as largest NGO partner. Centralized, mechanized kitchens cooking and delivering meals at scale. Public-private partnership model.
what_worked: Effective PPP with Indian government enabling massive scale
Harvard Business School studied the model (2007, 2017)
Gandhi Peace Prize 2016 and BBC Global Food Champion 2019
what_didnt_work: Dependency on government scheme continuity and funding
case_studies.key_lesson: Technology-driven, government-partnered models can address child hunger at scale. Nutrition and education create a powerful dual impact.

case_studies.title: SEWA: Two Million Informal Women Workers Organized
case_studies.problem_statement: Self-employed women in the informal economy lack access to healthcare, childcare, insurance, pensions, and banking.
case_studies.the_model: Trade union for informal women workers. Dual approach: 'Struggle' (advocacy) and 'Development' (services). SEWA Cooperative Bank for savings, microcredit, insurance. 50+ worker cooperatives. Co-founded WIEGO at Harvard Kennedy School.
what_worked: Combining advocacy with direct service provision
Member ownership in SEWA Bank — members are bankers, board, shareholders
Childcare as critical enabler increasing women's income by 50%
what_didnt_work: Microcredit criticized for introducing women to volatile capitalist system
Difficulty pushing higher wages in rural areas due to excess labor supply
Most low-income households didn't qualify for housing loans
case_studies.key_lesson: Empowering women requires both practical needs (income, health, childcare) and strategic needs (leadership, rights). Member ownership builds sustainability.

case_studies.title: SELCO India: Solar Energy for the Rural Poor
case_studies.problem_statement: Poor rural households lack energy access, limiting productivity, education, and economic opportunity. Conventional energy financing excludes low-income households.
case_studies.the_model: For-profit social enterprise in solar energy. 25% down payment plus affordable monthly installments within a family's budget. One-year warranty extension, free service, 90-day money-back guarantee.
what_worked: Affordable financial model making solar accessible to low-income households
Won Ashden Awards ('Green Oscars') twice — 2005 and 2007
Demonstrated viability of for-profit rural energy markets
what_didnt_work: Wikipedia article flagged for promotional content
case_studies.key_lesson: Creative financing can bridge the energy access gap. For-profit social enterprise can work in rural markets if payment matches income patterns.

case_studies.title: Jaipur Foot: $45 Prosthetics for the Developing World
case_studies.problem_statement: Existing prosthetics don't allow barefoot walking, squatting, cross-legged sitting, or working in muddy fields — all common daily activities in poorer regions.
case_studies.the_model: Low-cost rubber-based prosthetic leg for below-knee amputations. Rubber core, wooden block, vulcanised rubber coating. Costs $45 to make, lasts 2-5 years. Distributed free with government financial aid.
what_worked: Culturally adapted design allowing squatting and use on uneven terrain
Free distribution through BMVSS with government support
Used in low-income countries and war zones including Afghanistan landmine victims
Jaipur Knee with Stanford named Time's best invention 2009
what_didnt_work: Inferior to carbon fiber prosthetics in durability
Limited to household ambulation, not sports
case_studies.key_lesson: Context-appropriate design matters more than technical sophistication. A $45 prosthetic you can squat in beats a $10,000 one you can't.

case_studies.title: Aga Khan Foundation: Multi-Sector Development Across 17 Countries
case_studies.problem_statement: Poverty, hunger, illiteracy, and ill health in the poorest parts of South/Central Asia, Africa, and the Middle East.
case_studies.the_model: Long-term solutions across early childhood, education, health, agriculture, civil society, enterprise, and climate resilience. Coordinates with sister agencies in the Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN). The AKRSP model replicated through Pakistan's Rural Support Programmes Network.
what_worked: Innovative approaches designed for replicability across regions
Coordination among AKDN sister agencies multiplying impact
AKRSP model successfully replicated in Pakistan
2005 Global Development Network award for most innovative project
what_didnt_work: Large institutional structure may face agility challenges
case_studies.key_lesson: Long-term, multi-sector approaches with replicable models achieve broad reach. Design for replicability from the start.

case_studies.title: BRAC: World's Largest NGO, 126M+ People Reached
case_studies.problem_statement: Systemic poverty in Bangladesh requiring integrated approaches to microfinance, education, health, and disaster relief.
case_studies.the_model: Integrated development model combining microfinance, non-formal education, community health workers, and ultra-poor graduation programs. Operates across 13 countries in Asia, Africa, and the Caribbean.
what_didnt_work: Dependency on donor funding for some programs
case_studies.key_lesson: Poverty requires integrated solutions — microfinance alone is not enough. Combining financial services with health, education, and social development creates lasting change.

case_studies.title: Grameen Bank: Microcredit Pioneer
case_studies.problem_statement: The poor lacked access to credit because they had no collateral, trapping them in cycles of poverty.
case_studies.the_model: Microcredit through solidarity lending groups. No collateral required. Trust-based system. 95% repayment rate. Focus on women borrowers (97% of borrowers). Sixteen Decisions social pledges.
what_didnt_work: Difficulty replicating model outside Bangladesh initially
case_studies.key_lesson: The poor are creditworthy. Trust-based lending without collateral can achieve 95% repayment when combined with community support structures.

case_studies.title: Ashoka: Social Entrepreneurship Network, 4000+ Fellows
case_studies.problem_statement: Systemic social problems need entrepreneurs with innovative solutions, but there was no global network to support them.
case_studies.the_model: Elects leading social entrepreneurs as Fellows, providing stipends, peer networks, and organizational support. Over 4,000 fellows in 90+ countries.
what_worked: Focus on systemic change over charity
what_didnt_work: Highly selective — many qualified social entrepreneurs not elected
case_studies.key_lesson: Social entrepreneurs who achieve systemic change don't just solve problems — they transform the systems that create them.

case_studies.title: Water.org: WaterCredit Microfinance for Water Access
case_studies.problem_statement: 780 million people lack access to safe water. Traditional charity models for water projects are not sustainable at scale.
case_studies.the_model: WaterCredit microfinance model: partners with local financial institutions to offer small loans for water connections and sanitation. Repayment funds more loans.
what_didnt_work: Depends on functioning local financial systems
Not suitable for areas with no banking infrastructure
case_studies.key_lesson: Microfinance can work for water access, not just income generation. Small loans for water connections create a self-sustaining funding cycle.

case_studies.title: Khan Academy: Free Global Education Platform
case_studies.problem_statement: Quality education is inaccessible to billions due to cost, geography, and teacher shortages.
case_studies.the_model: Free online education platform with thousands of video lessons, practice exercises, and personalized learning dashboards. Available in 14+ languages. Partnered with College Board for SAT/AP prep.
what_didnt_work: Limited for early literacy without adult guidance
case_studies.key_lesson: World-class education can be delivered for free at massive scale. The key is making it accessible, personalized, and engaging.

case_studies.title: Habitat for Humanity: Sweat Equity Housing Model
case_studies.problem_statement: Millions of families lack access to safe, decent, affordable housing.
case_studies.the_model: Volunteer labor and sweat equity model: homeowners contribute their own labor to building their homes. Zero-interest mortgages. Habitat ReStores sell donated materials to fund operations.
what_worked: Sweat equity builds ownership and dignity
what_didnt_work: Land costs in urban areas are prohibitive
case_studies.key_lesson: Sweat equity transforms housing from charity into partnership. When families invest their own labor, they build both homes and dignity.

case_studies.title: Malala Fund: Girls Education Advocacy
case_studies.problem_statement: 130 million girls worldwide are out of school due to conflict, poverty, discrimination, and child marriage.
case_studies.the_model: Advocacy and funding model: invests in local education activists and organizations in regions where girls face the greatest barriers. Advocates for policy change at global level.
what_worked: Amplifies local voices rather than imposing solutions
what_didnt_work: Scale of funding vs. the scale of the problem
case_studies.key_lesson: Advocacy backed by personal story and local partnerships can influence global policy. The most effective education investments fund local leaders, not external programs.

case_studies.title: Bachpan Bachao Andolan: 138,000+ Children Rescued
case_studies.problem_statement: Millions of children in India trapped in child labor, trafficking, and slavery.
case_studies.the_model: Rescue operations, legal advocacy, and community mobilization. Rescued 138,000+ children. Led to ILO Convention 182 on worst forms of child labor. GoodWeave certification for rug industry.
what_worked: Legal advocacy leading to policy change
Global March Against Child Labour (103 countries)
what_didnt_work: Child labor persists despite decades of work
Rescue is only the first step — rehabilitation is harder
case_studies.key_lesson: Combining direct action (rescue) with systemic change (laws, certification) creates lasting impact. Certification models like GoodWeave create market incentives against child labor.
